articles.title: Tata Motors acquires majority stake in Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco for 3.43 billion euros
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tata Motors on Friday acquired an 89.42% stake in Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco Group for around 3.43 billion euros after the initial
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tata Motors on Friday acquired an 89.42% stake in Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco Group for around 3.43 billion euros after the initial settlement of its cash tender offer, taking control of the European company as the acquisition process continues.The deal makes Iveco an indirect subsidiary of Tata Motors and marks the Indian automaker’s biggest acquisition since it bought Jaguar Land Rover from Ford in 2008. Iveco reported revenue of Rs 1,42,471 crore and employs around 33,000 people across 16 industrial sites and 22 research and development centres.In a joint statement on Friday, the companies said TML CV Holdings B.V., an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Motors, had acquired 238,157,212 common shares of Iveco, representing approximately 89.42% of its common share capital, excluding treasury shares.“Iveco Group has now become part of Tata Motors,” the company said, PTI reported. The settlement follows the completion of the acceptance period for Tata Motors’ voluntary cash tender offer, under which it offered 14.4 euros per share for Iveco’s common shares.The acceptance period will reopen for five trading days, from November 2 to November 6, 2026, giving shareholders another opportunity to tender their shares. The settlement for shares tendered during this period is scheduled for November 13.Tata Motors had initially offered 14.10 euros per share before raising the price by 0.30 euros to 14.40 euros, including dividends, on October 9.As part of the acquisition, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran has been appointed chairperson and senior non-executive director of Iveco. Olof Persson will continue as chief executive officer.Tata Motors executives P B Balaji and Girish Wagh have joined the board as non-independent, non-executive directors. Guenter Butschek and Charles Nichols have been appointed independent, non-executive directors.Iveco has also reconstituted its board committees, amended its corporate governance documents and repurchased all special voting shares.The companies said details of the next steps following the offer, including the voluntary purchase procedure, a Dutch-law squeeze-out process or a post-offer demerger and liquidation, would be communicated in due course.Tata Motors announced plans in 2025 to acquire Iveco, excluding its defence business, in a deal valued at around 3.8 billion euros (nearly Rs 38,240 crore). The transaction was to be carried out through TML CV Holdings Pte Ltd.The acquisition is aimed at expanding Tata Motors’ global commercial vehicle presence by combining its operations with Iveco’s established international network and product portfolio.You use AI every day. articles.title: The Binance hack is way bigger than any other known heist in the crypto world
articles.summary: The estimated $6.3 billion theft reported Thursday by crypto exchange Binance isn't the first time the industry has dealt with a major, unexpected incident.
articles.body:
The estimated $6.3 billion theft reported Thursday by crypto exchange Binance isn't the first time the industry has dealt with a major, unexpected incident in which large sums of customer assets are frozen , spurring a rout in crypto stocks.

It may bring to mind crypto's more turbulent days, such as the collapse of FTX, though in that full-on meltdown , with an initial shortfall of $8 billion to $8.9 billion, the Binance rival's own founder, Sam Bankman-Fried, was charged with the heist. Bankman-Fried was convicted of fraud in 2024 and sentenced to 25 years in prison.

The Binance hack has rattled crypto markets: Bitcoin ( BTC ), other digital assets, and related stocks have sunk over the last 24 hours. The company has temporarily suspended customer withdrawals, and outside investigators are racing to track down the stolen funds. The company said it has successfully frozen 44% of stolen funds with the help of stablecoin issuers and "will cover all losses" from the incident.

As far as comparable hacks go, this most recent theft towers over the rest in terms of scale. Here are four major crypto thefts you may not have heard of.

Nearly $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit in February 2025

Hackers linked to North Korea stole nearly $1.5 billion in ether from cryptocurrency exchange Bybit. The attackers manipulated a transaction approval process, allowing them to redirect assets from a supposedly secure wallet.

$625 million on Ronin Network compromised in March 2022

Hackers compromised the security infrastructure of Ronin Network, a blockchain connected to Axie Infinity, a then-popular online crypto game. Hackers stole approximately 173,600 ether and 25.5 million USDC tokens . US authorities weeks later attributed the attack to North Korean hackers , known as the Lazarus Group.

$611 million nabbed from Poly Network in August 2021

In 2021, an attacker exploited a vulnerability in Poly Network, a platform designed to transfer crypto across different blockchains. In an unusual development, the attacker subsequently returned nearly all of the stolen assets, claiming they did it " for fun " and to expose a software vulnerability.

$3.5 billion lost from Chinese bitcoin mining pool LuBian in December 2020 (Unconfirmed)

A crypto wallet tied to a little-known Chinese bitcoin mining pool called LuBian may have been the victim of what would be the second-largest crypto theft ever recorded after Binance's breach.

LuBian apparently lost more than 127,426 BTC after hackers potentially exploited weaknesses in how the company generated its private keys, according to findings reported by blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence. The suspected theft wasn't identified until August of last year.

articles.title: Intel stock plunges nearly 30%, on pace for its worst day since 1974
articles.summary: A weak outlook has Intel on pace for one of its worst days in half a century.
articles.body:
Intel's data center business just grew almost 80% in a year. Its outlook for the fourth quarter has the stock on pace for its worst day in more than half a century, erasing nearly $150 billion in market value Friday.

Intel ( INTC ) stock fell as much as 30% in early trading Friday after the chipmaker's forecast for the final three months of the year came in well short of Wall Street's expectations.

That would top every day since at least 1973, according to Yahoo Finance calculations from Norgate Data closing prices going back to May 1973. The previous worst was July 5, 1974, when Intel fell nearly 30%. Its 26% plunge on Aug. 2, 2024, is now third.

The sell-off caps a wild year. Intel stock nearly quadrupled from the start of 2026 to its June 22 record. Even after Friday's drop, it's still up more than 70% this year, but it has given back about half its value since that peak.

The selloff is also costing Washington. Intel's drop has shaved more than $10 billion off the value of the US government's 9.9% stake, which it bought last August at $20.47 a share. Even so, the stake is still worth about three times what the government paid.

It has also broken below the $80 zone that held at its July low, and it's on track to close below where it stood before April 24, when Intel had its best day since at least 1973, a gain of about 24%.

The quarter itself was strong. Intel topped estimates with adjusted earnings per share of $0.52, and data center revenue jumped to $7.3 billion.

The outlook is what broke the stock. Intel expects fourth quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below the roughly $17 billion analysts expected, and earnings per share of $0.25 against forecasts of $0.43.

The PC market is the problem . AI data centers are soaking up the world's memory chips, pushing up prices for laptops and desktops. Intel now expects PC shipments to fall about 12% this year and another 10% in 2027. An accident at its Israel factory will cost about $300 million in fourth quarter revenue on top of that.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon called the outlook "(in a word) terrible" and cut his price target to $75 from $110.

PC makers Dell ( DELL ) and HP ( HPQ ) slid too, adding to a tech stock rout that has hit Alphabet ( GOOGL , GOOG ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) after their reports this week.

Intel said the PC slump won't let up until memory supply and prices return to normal.

"Rebuilding Intel is going to be a multiyear journey, and I remain firmly committed to making it happen," CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Thursday's earnings call.

articles.title: Alphabet's October wipeout hits $766 billion, its worst month ever
articles.summary: Alphabet's $477 billion weekly loss at Friday's low outpaced SpaceX, Intel, Nvidia and Amazon combined, capping its worst month ever.
articles.body:
Big Tech's brutal week had one clear epicenter. At its low Friday, Alphabet ( GOOGL ) had lost $477 billion in market value for the week, more than SpaceX, Intel, Nvidia and Amazon combined.

That would be the Google parent's worst week ever and the second-biggest weekly wipeout for any US-listed stock, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Only Nvidia ( NVDA ) has lost more, about $552 billion in the week of Jan. 27, 2025, when China's DeepSeek rattled AI investors. Alphabet's previous worst was about $386 billion in the week ended June 26.

Most of the damage came Thursday, when Alphabet lost $475 billion in a single session after its third quarter results . Friday's slide wiped out the gains the stock had made earlier in the week.

October looks even worse. At Friday's low, Alphabet had shed about $766 billion in market value this month, the second-biggest monthly loss ever for a US-listed company. Only SpaceX ( SPCX ) has lost more, about $822 billion in July. Alphabet's October loss is nearly double its previous worst month, about $420 billion in February 2025.

In percentage terms, the stock was down nearly 19% for October at its low, steeper than any month since it went public in 2004. Its previous worst was an 18.5% drop in November 2008. For the week, it was down nearly 13%, its worst since August 2011.

SpaceX, Intel ( INTC ) and Nvidia each lost more than $100 billion in market value this week. Intel fell as much as 30% Friday after a weak outlook, its steepest drop in decades . Amazon ( AMZN ) shed about $70 billion for the week after reporting results Thursday. Some software names fell harder in percentage terms, with ServiceNow ( NOW ) and Fortinet ( FTNT ) down roughly 25% to 33%.

Not all of that money left the market. Eli Lilly ( LLY ), Tesla ( TSLA ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) added about $370 billion in combined value, even as the Magnificent Seven stumbled .

UBS's chief investment office argued against heading for the exits. "Further volatility does not make retreating from markets an effective way to protect portfolios from potential drawdowns, in our view," Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, CIO Americas and global head of equities, wrote Friday. "We continue to see scope for equity gains overall and believe investors should focus on building a resilient portfolio that includes exposure beyond tech."

Friday's close will settle the records. A close at or below $280.50 would lock in Alphabet's worst month since its IPO in percentage terms. To take Nvidia's weekly record in dollars, the stock would need to close near $273, down nearly 15% for the week.

articles.title: 'Sentiment will take a hit': Binance $6.3 billion hack rattles bitcoin, crypto market
articles.summary: Crypto assets took a hit this week after Binance's $6.3 billion hack, but the sour sentiment should be short-lived, analysts say.
articles.body:
Binance's $6.3 billion hack this week rattled the crypto market, with nearly every digital asset taking a leg lower on Friday. While the knee-jerk reaction was to sell, industry watchers see the move lower in assets as temporary.

"Binance has committed to covering the losses from its own funds and reserves, so we shouldn't see contagion from this exploit," Nikhil Raghuveera, co-founder of on-chain compliance firm Predicate, told Yahoo Finance.

"Sentiment will take a hit, however," he added.

Crypto assets across the board were mostly lower on Friday, as seen on Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data .

Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) prices tumbled to around $77,000 on Friday, while ether ( ETH-USD ) also dropped 4% to around $2,200. Altcoins Solana ( SOL-USD ) and Binance's native token ( BNB-USD ) also plummeted 7%.

Crypto-related stocks, however, also declined. Shares of Circle ( CRCL ) and trading platforms Coinbase ( COIN ) and Robinhood ( HOOD ) all tumbled. Digital-asset Treasury giant Strategy ( MSTR ) stock also sank. (Disclosure: Yahoo Finance has a partnership with Coinbase.)

Customer withdrawals have been temporarily suspended, and on Friday, co-CEO Richard Teng promised that the exchange will cover all losses from its funds.

"Your assets are safe," Teng said on social media.

Shortly after the hack was announced, the exchange confirmed $3 billion in assets, or about half of the funds impacted, were frozen. Stablecoin issuers Tether froze $1.567 billion in USDT, Circle froze $800 million, and World Liberty Financial froze $27 million in USD1, according to their CEOs.

Binance hacked for record $6.3B, withdrawals suspended after "complex attack"

What Binance users should do right now following major hack

Binance's $6.3 billion hack: How the biggest crypto heist unfolded

"The real systemic concern would be a shortfall in customer assets that forces Binance to liquidate reserves, accelerates withdrawals, causes counterparties to pull credit, and creates a reflexive deleveraging cycle across crypto," Fundstrat head of digital assets Sean Farrell said.

Assuming frozen stablecoins are ultimately returned, the remainder is roughly $3.3 billion. Binance's emergency fund of roughly $1.2 billion, held in bitcoin, would cover roughly a third, with the balance coming from the exchange's own balance sheet.

"That removes what I would view as the most dangerous tail risk," Farrell said.

articles.title: Stock market today: Nasdaq dives over 3%, S&P 500 and Dow tank as AI reckoning grips Wall Street
articles.summary: US stocks were on track for their worst day since June as AI fears sparked a brutal sell-off.
articles.body: US stocks plunged in the final trading day of the month as earnings from Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) this week rekindled concerns about the amount of money Big Tech is spending on its AI ambitions.The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) tumbled 3.3% as a tech-fueled sell-off intensified. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) fell 1.2%, or over 600 points, while those on the S&P 500 (^GSPC) dropped 2.2%. The Nasdaq is on track for its worst month since March 2025.Stocks fell for the second day in a row after Amazon and Alphabet posted rare earnings misses, renewing concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom. Amazon shares fell 2%, while Alphabet continued to erase market value after its stock suffered its worst day in over 20 years.Intel (INTC) also suffered a brutal reaction to its earnings report, dropping 30% in premarket trading after the company's Q4 outlook came up short.One bright spot in the market was ExxonMobil (XOM) and Chevron (CVX), whose stocks briefly touched record highs after the oil majors reported that their earnings were boosted as refining margins widened amid the war in the Middle East. Pharmaceutical company AstraZeneca (AZN) also reported an earnings beat before the opening bell.While earnings remain in focus, oil prices rebounded higher, putting additional pressure on markets. Brent crude futures (BZ=F) rose to $113 per barrel, while WTI crude (CL=F) reached $104 per barrel.Bitcoin (BTC-USD) prices tumbled more than 5% as crypto assets were rattled following a $6.3 billion hack on cryptocurrency exchange Binance, marking the largest heist of its kind in history.
